answer: A head clears the wharf only by carrying one real person's published admission of a fault they committed themselves: their own words, tied to no claim and no victim, so it can neither be aimed at a flattering job nor lent to a sibling. Each person may make one admission in a life; the wharf burns its ember into the ledger and marks it spent for good. The summit roll lists every spent admission beside its author, so a farm's tenth head needs a tenth person willing to publish a mistake of their own, and honest people stop offering once one address gathers a column.
